title: attribution/v1 audit-result
description: Output of an attribution audit over a time window: how many sessions were exactly attributed to a single task_run vs. unbound/mixed/orphaned, and whether the window is eligible for research use. See docs/protocols/attribution-v1.md. There is deliberately no standalone session-count field anywhere in `sessions` -- every count (including the total number of sessions measured) is derived by summing the five lists' lengths, never independently declared and therefore never able to drift out of sync with the lists themselves. Rules this schema alone cannot express, enforced instead as semantic checks in verify-fixtures.mjs: (1) `research_eligible` MUST be false if `violations` is non-empty (fail-closed, not advisory) -- see 'Rejected designs' for why this MUST is not softened to a warning. (2) `tokens.exact_attributed`/`tokens.total_measured` MUST be null, never 0, when all five `sessions` lists are empty (null-not-zero: 'nothing was measured' and 'zero tokens were measured' are different facts). (3) `tokens.exact_attributed` MUST equal the sum of `sessions.exactly_attributed[].tokens`. (4) the five lists' session_ids MUST be pairwise disjoint. (5) every session_id in `unbound`/`mixed`/`orphan_usage`/`measurement_incomplete` MUST have a matching `violations[]` entry (same session_id, the corresponding reason_code) and vice versa -- a session sitting in one of these lists with no matching violation (or a violation referencing a session absent from its list) is rejected.

sessions.description: exactly_attributed = sessions cleanly resolved to exactly one task_run (the accounting principle this whole protocol exists to certify), carried as {session_id, tokens} pairs so tokens.exact_attributed can be independently verified as their sum. The other four are disjoint session_id lists explaining every session NOT in exactly_attributed. There is no `measured` count field -- the total number of sessions audited is always sessions.exactly_attributed.length + the four lists' combined length, derived, never separately declared (sol architect-review must4: a separately-declared count is a second source of truth that can silently drift from the lists it's supposed to summarize).

tokens.description: exact_attributed = sum of sessions.exactly_attributed[].tokens, independently verified (verify-fixtures.mjs recomputes the sum and rejects on mismatch -- the field is never just trusted). total_measured = total tokens across every measured session (exactly_attributed + unbound + mixed + orphan_usage + measurement_incomplete), still just a measured total -- NEVER a mixed-session apportionment (see docs/protocols/attribution-v1.md 'Rejected designs': splitting a mixed session's tokens by time ratio between its tasks is a fabrication this protocol forbids, not merely discourages). total_measured MUST be >= exact_attributed (sol architect-review 2nd round must A3 -- the exactly-attributed sessions' usage is a subset of everything measured, so the total can never be smaller than the part). Both fields are null, not 0, when all five `sessions` lists are empty.

violations.description: sol architect-review 2nd round must A1: session_id is required (not optional) on every violation -- this schema's reason_code closed set is exactly the four session-keyed reasons (UNBOUND_SESSION/MULTI_TASK_BINDING/ORPHAN_USAGE/MEASUREMENT_INCOMPLETE), so every violation here is inherently about some specific session. A violation with no session_id could not be checked against sessions.{unbound,mixed,orphan_usage,measurement_incomplete} by verify-fixtures.mjs's bidirectional correspondence check, letting it slip through unverified -- making it required closes that hole structurally.
